title: Gold curriculum design note (optional structured format)
description: Optional machine-checkable structure for a design note (see DESIGN_NOTES_TEMPLATE.md). Design notes explain why an example was written and are never read by the training pipeline. This is NOT the trained-data schema — see training_data.schema.json for that. A curator may write a design note as free-form prose following DESIGN_NOTES_TEMPLATE.md, or as JSON validating against this schema; both are equally acceptable, this just gives the JSON option a checkable shape.

example_id.description: e.g. G1.2-001 — matches the batch-version-number convention in DESIGN_NOTES_TEMPLATE.md.

curriculum_level.description: Curriculum level name (see TAXONOMY.md's Difficulty categories). Not the trained difficulty value — see training_data.schema.json's difficulty enum (easy|medium|hard|expert) for that.

lesson.description: The one recovery skill this example teaches — should match its category in the trained data.

author_intent.description: What this example is meant to prove the model can (or currently cannot) do.

scenario.description: The real-world situation this note is set in.

boundary_evidence.description: For each topic boundary in this example: what signals it and how confident that signal is. See TAXONOMY.md's Boundary categories and Confidence categories.

evidence.description: What in the text actually signals this boundary.

failure_modes.description: Which of TAXONOMY.md's Failure categories this example is designed to expose.

hallucinations_to_watch_for.description: Specific plausible-sounding but false things a reviewer should check the model didn't invent for this example.

why_this_example_is_at_this_point_in_the.description: What makes this example harder or different from the ones before it.

expected_recovery.description: What a correct output looks like, in plain terms — not the literal trained-data JSON.
